notes: SUMMARY: 42 images, all public domain, CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA (no NC/ND, no fair use); every item verified=true. Per era: walls 4, castle 5, letalone 5, rights 5, dataprotection 7, cookies 4, surveillance 8, agents 4. Licences: Public domain 12, CC BY 2.0 8, CC BY-SA 3.0 7, CC0 4, CC BY-SA 4.0 4, CC BY 3.0 3, CC BY 4.0 2, CC BY-SA 3.0 DE 1, CC BY-SA 2.0 1. Sources: Wikimedia Commons file pages (incl. uploads from the Walters Art Museum, Rijksmuseum, Wellcome Collection, Library of Congress, NARA/DPLA, U.S. Census Bureau, Bundesarchiv, Landesarchiv Baden-Württemberg, Council of Europe, FDR Library, Tekniska museet and Flickr CC uploads) plus the Metropolitan Museum Open Access API (Hogarth's Wilkes, Bartolozzi's Camden). METHOD: the Commons API answered HTTP 429 from this shared IP throughout, so each licence was read from the Licensing/Permission section of the Commons file page HTML (fetched with a descriptive User-Agent) and quoted in rightsEvidence; LoC records were read through the loc.gov JSON API (?fo=json), Met records through collectionapi.metmuseum.org, the Oxyrhynchus papyrus through the Wellcome catalogue API. Every picture was viewed after download and alt text written from the image; captions use only facts on the record page (or text legible in the image itself, flagged in rightsEvidence). LOCAL MIRRORS: assets/media/<id>.jpg, JPEG q82, fitted within 960x1200 px, opened and verified with Pillow. upload.wikimedia.org now serves only standard thumbnail widths (250/330/500/960) and returns 429 for original files, so for originals narrower than 960 px the 500 px thumbnail was used (hollerith, snowden, council-of-europe plaque, census demo, stasi-erfurt, genai diagram); the Phorm SVG was rendered by Wikimedia to PNG and flattened onto white. thumbCheck records a final HTTP check of each thumbUrl (40 of 42 returned 200; 2 hit rate limits). The two metmuseum.org object pages (sourceUrl for Wilkes and Camden) answer 429 to scripts; their API records were read instead and are given as upstreamUrl. COORDINATES: place of making/depiction per the record, or the camera location on the file page where one is given; two conceptual diagrams (phorm-tracking-cookie-diagram-2008, generative-ai-agent-architecture-diagram) have lat/lng null on purpose. GAPS AND JUDGEMENT CALLS: no openly licensed photo of Lou Montulli, of the IEEE Operations Center (Piscataway), of a 1983 census-boycott poster, of the 1950 ECHR signing, or of anything branded MyTerms/IEEE 7012 was found; the 1987 Freiburg census demonstration stands in for the boycott movement. Samuel D. Warren omitted: the Commons 'Samuel Dennis Warren' portraits show an older man and most likely depict his father, the paper manufacturer (1817-1888). William Pitt the Elder omitted: available images were British Museum prints or National Portrait Gallery reproductions carrying third-party copyright-claim warnings; NPG London files were avoided for the same reason (Camden taken from the Met instead). The Olmstead bootlegging photos (MOHAI) were avoided because their credit line says 'All Rights Reserved' despite a PD tag. The Taft Court photos (LoC) are undated ('between 1905 and 1945') and were skipped. The Commons description of the Bill of Rights says ten articles became part of the Constitution 'in 1794'; ratification was completed in 1791, so the caption avoids the date. Several person-portraits carry Commons personality-rights warnings (usual for living people). HOUSEKEEPING: the scratchpad is shared by concurrent researchers; around 10:24 another slice's data-protection events were accidentally written into this file through a same-named helper script (add.py). They were removed from media.json, saved unchanged to the scratchpad as RECOVERED-dataprotection-records-from-media-json.json, and research/dataprotection.json has since been written by its owner. assets/media/latanya-sweeney-knight-news-challenge-2017.jpg belongs to the personas-researchers slice, not to this file.

images.title: How Phorm copied its tracking cookie across websites
images.caption: A 2008 diagram showing how Phorm's system, sitting inside an internet service provider's network, masqueraded as the websites a browser visited (here Bebo.com) in order to plant copies of its 'webwise' tracking cookie in each domain and pass requests to a profiler. It is based on the analysis published by Richard Clayton.
images.alt: Flow diagram: a user's browser on the left exchanges cookie-labelled arrows with a Phorm system box inside the ISP network, which masquerades as Bebo.com and Webwise.net and sends copies to a profiler
images.creator: Lostforwords
images.creditLine: Lostforwords / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
images.locationNote: No place recorded for the diagram (coordinates left empty on purpose). Richard Clayton's underlying analysis, 'The Phorm "Webwise" System' (4 April 2008, revised 18 May 2008), was published at the University of Cambridge Computer Laboratory: https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~rnc1/080518-phorm.pdf
images.rightsEvidence: Commons file page Licensing section: "Lostforwords, the copyright holder of this work, hereby publishes it under the following license: This file is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0 Unported license. Attribution: Lostforwords". Description: "A diagram showing how Phorm's system creates copies of its tracking cookie in each domain the browser fetches, based on the analysis published by Richard Clayton." Date 28 April 2008. SVG rendered by Wikimedia to PNG and flattened onto white for the local JPEG.
